name: P01 a paragraph of two lines has no line to scan (the count guard raised)
P02 a count of 1 is a paragraph the scan starts again for (the guard lowered to <)
P03 a count of 1 is a paragraph the scan starts again for (the guard lowered to <= 0)
P04 the paragraph's start is not floored at the first line
P05 a different list of lines is not a new paragraph
P06 a different start is not a new paragraph
P07 a different columns array is not a new paragraph
why: No document in 300,000 random and 4.4 million aimed ones tells it from the key (the columns of an open paragraph almost never change between two questions); the warm seeded row of the oracle kills it.

name: P08 a list that has become shorter is not a new paragraph
why: computeRegions never shortens bodyLines; the read-count row of the oracle kills it.

name: P09 the columns are not rooted at 0 and nothing else (the open columns dropped)
P10 the columns are not rooted at 0 (column 0 dropped)
why: Equivalent: `containerContentColumn` starts its base at 0 and keeps the deepest column not past the line's, so a 0 in the columns array changes no answer; the rooting is kept because it is the old expression's own `[0, ...columns]`.

name: P11 the first line of the paragraph is read too
P12 the second line of the paragraph is not read
P13 a new paragraph keeps the old answer
P14 the scan goes on past an interrupter and the last line decides
P15 the last line of the paragraph is not read
P16 every second line is read
P17 the line above the one due is read
P18 the answer is always no
P19 the answer is always yes
P20 the verdict of a line is inverted
P21 the columns are kept as a copy, so the key never matches (a clock mutant: every answer is right)
why: Every answer is right and every question rescans the paragraph: killed by the clock rows of pathological-inputs.test.ts (an interrupter far down a paragraph), and by the oracle's 200,000-question row, which never ends under it.

name: P22 the lines are kept as a copy, so the key never matches (a clock mutant: every answer is right)
why: As P21, for the lines array.

name: G01 the scan is asked for every line (the gate removed: a clock mutant)
why: The scan is asked for every line when the gate is gone, and it still answers the same and costs the same on every shape tried (pairs and triples of line forms, random documents: the memo makes each question one read), so the clock cannot see it. The 'how often the scan is asked' rows of paragraph-interrupt-wiring.test.ts count the questions and kill it.

name: G02 the scan is asked only for a level 1 underline
G03 the scan is asked only for a level 2 underline
G04 an interrupted paragraph keeps its whole title
G05 an uninterrupted paragraph loses its title
G06 an interrupted paragraph's title is 0 lines (the default, written as a number)
why: Equivalent: the scan answers true only for a paragraph of two lines or more, where `consecutiveBody === 1` is false and `defaultTitleLineCount` is 0.

name: G07 the scan reads the CommonMark entries' columns only
why: Found by Session 332's mutation run: no row told `columns()` from `commonmarkColumns()` until the wiring rows for an indented bullet followed by a letter-marker or definition item (a pandoc-only container column that makes the bullet an interrupter) were added.

name: G08 the scan is told the run length and not the title length
why: Equivalent: `wholeParagraph` is `consecutiveBody` under a CommonMark reader unless the run opens a non-paragraph, and then it is `defaultTitleLineCount`, which both spellings return.

name: G09 a new scan for every question (a clock mutant: every answer is right)
G10 the four columns of an underline start at the column 0
G11 the four columns of an underline run the other way
G12 the underline of a CommonMark reader is asked of the other readers
G13 setextLevel takes a level 1 whatever the underline
